comment: T4 baseline (docs/TESTING.md). `load` and `context` in `taken` are the conditions of the MILLISECONDS rows — CPU load over 1-second samples before the run, and what invoked the binary. P2's phase-end measurement filled them from a controlled interleaved A/B against the P1 tree `46d939b`, six alternating pairs per scene. UI present is 12.13 ms (11.71–12.70), against P1's 21.36 ms (19.83–23.23): one UI draw and 48 890 instances make the complete 20 000-node scene 43% faster, but the roadmap's optimistic 2.0 ms prediction was not met. Sprite present is 1.77 ms (1.74–1.79), against P1's 2.11 ms (2.04–2.23), so guardrail 8 holds. GLYPH MODE AND THE WHITE-TEXEL CARD, 2026-09-22. The label's shaped quads are UI instances in glyph mode and the card binds the glyph atlas view, so the alternating card/label pair that held ui.draws at 20000 is one run now. Arithmetic for every moved row. ui.draws 20000 -> 1, P2's exit number met at its floor. ui.vertices 233340 -> 0: the labels were the last vertices and their quads are instances. ui.uiInstances 10000 -> 48890 = 10000 cards + 38890 glyph quads. ui.uploadBytes 8546880 -> 5280120, exactly 48890 x 108 B. ui.uploads 2 -> 1: no vertex stream left, one append. retainedNodes UNCHANGED at 10000 - the mesh stays on the node for the colour-pipeline fallback and this file still counts it.

taken.renderer: the unified UI pipeline: cards and glyph quads are instances; one run, one draw
taken.load: 11.77% CPU mean over five 1 s samples before the run
taken.context: interleaved A/B vs 46d939b, six alternating pairs per scene
